source.title: Benign Overfitting in Two-layer ReLU Convolutional Neural Networks
source.authors: Yi-Wen Kou; Zixiang Chen; Yuanzhou Chen; Quanquan Gu

page_placements.theme: Training fit does not determine generalization or representation quality

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies whether a two-layer ReLU CNN can fit label-flipped training data while generalizing, using theoretical risk bounds and synthetic-data experiments. It does not test completely random labels or the progressions specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern label-flipping noise at p=0.1 in the synthetic experiment and theoretical bounds for p≤1/C. They do not test completely random labels, a noise-rate sweep from none to all, or the other version-specific conditions.
record.test_reason: The theoretical learning dynamics bear on V6: signal learning and noise memorization grow concurrently with a time-invariant order of their coefficient ratio. This qualifies a general signal-first, noise-later account in the paper's restricted synthetic setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under stated distributional and regularity conditions, gradient descent achieves arbitrarily small training loss, with test error close to the label-noise rate in the favorable regime and at least p+0.1 in the unfavorable regime.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes a two-layer ReLU CNN trained by gradient descent on synthetic patch-structured data with label-flipping noise. It does not use the original random-label image experiments or their setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Theoretical test-risk result depends on the signal-to-noise and sample-size condition: n∥µ∥⁴₂ relative to σp⁴d. The synthetic experiment reports a heatmap over dimension and signal strength.

fits_no_version.finding: At p=0.1, n=20, d=100, and signal norm 5, training loss approaches zero while estimated test error reaches the Bayes error of 0.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A two-layer ReLU CNN can interpolate partially corrupted synthetic training data while attaining approximately Bayes-optimal test error.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: The experiment uses a synthetic dataset with n=20 and one reported label-flip rate; test error is estimated from 1000 test points. No uncertainty interval is stated. The broader bounds rely on restrictive regularity and distribution conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows: Figure 1 reports a test-error heatmap across dimension and signal strength but the supplied text gives no numerical values for its individual cells.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Fitting wholly unstructured inputs; each input here retains a label-dependent signal patch alongside its Gaussian noise patch.
Perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error across corruption fractions from none to all.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation.
Clean-versus-corrupted sample accuracy trajectories on real datasets, completely random labels, and generalization to deep networks outside the stated theoretical conditions.

missing.what: Record the theoretical training dynamics: signal coefficients increase while noise-memorization coefficients increase, with gamma/sum(rho) remaining of order signal_norm_squared/(d*noise_variance) throughout training. This establishes concurrent growth at the coefficient level, without directly measuring clean-versus-corrupted accuracy ordering.
missing.locator: Section 5.1, Proposition 5.2; Appendix D, Lemmas D.7–D.8.

record.verdict_notes: The time-invariant ratio is an order bound, not an exact equality; it does not alone prove identical clean and corrupted accuracy trajectories. Neither existing row directly records the theoretical result bearing on V6.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labeling of the training set, including test error at chance.
Training-time comparison with true labels and convergence slowdown as the corrupted-label fraction grows.
Shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A sweep from no corruption to all labels corrupted, with training and test error tracked across the sweep.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and their removal.
Whether real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels, or whether learning differs over training.
